title: Tingley's problem
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's solution (2026) of Tingley's problem: every surjective isometry between the unit spheres of nonzero real Banach spaces, and in fact of real normed spaces, extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry, the radial map. The first lesson treats supports, radial contact with the sphere and convexity of the norm along lines, proves the Mazur-Ulam theorem by Vaisala's reflection argument, and reduces the problem to the vanishing of the defect, the largest error of the radial map between two radii. The second constructs ultrapowers of normed spaces to make a positive defect attained, and proves Kuratowski's measure of noncompactness lemmas, Schauder's fixed-point theorem from Brouwer's and Darbo's theorem. The third builds a return map on directions, propagates extremality along common supports to an invariant closed convex set on which the map contracts noncompactness, and obtains aligned chords from Darbo's theorem. The fourth rules out aligned chords by a secant estimate, a radial perturbation and a convexity argument, and proves the theorem.
prerequisites: foundations-of-von-neumann-algebras lesson hahn-banach-baire-and-the-basic-theorems-on-banach-spaces (Theorem 1.1, Zorn's lemma; Corollary 2.3, Hahn-Banach for normed spaces); lesson weak-topologies-tychonoff-banach-alaoglu-mazur-bipolars-krein-milman-and-eberlein-smulian (Theorem 3.1, only in an exercise)
index-theory-of-elliptic-operators lesson lebesgue-s-covering-theorem-and-the-dimension-of-cubes (Corollary 1.2, Brouwer's theorem for compact convex subsets of R^n, from core course D60)
real analysis: intermediate value theorem, convex functions of one variable, compactness in R^n
